correctness.rationale: For \(Q=y^2+z^2\), direct differentiation in the inspected source tree gives exactly \(LQ=-2cy^2-2bz\), so stationarity yields \(b\mathbb E[z]=-c\mathbb E[y^2]\). Stationarity of \(z\) gives \(\mathbb E[xy]=b\), which rules out \(y=0\) almost surely and makes the mean-height inequality strict. Any nonempty compact invariant set would carry an invariant probability measure, so containment in \(z\ge0\) contradicts the negative mean. The divergence is exactly \(-a-c+kz\); compact support makes the derivative cocycle bounded, and Liouville plus ergodicity identifies the Lyapunov-exponent sum with the mean divergence. Substituting the stationary height balance proves the displayed law.

value.rationale: The source interprets hyperchaos partly through numerical Lyapunov spectra and state-dependent divergence. The audited balance turns that into an exact recurrent-statistics law, fixes the sign of the mean height, excludes an entire half-space for compact recurrence and gives a consistency equation for any claimed asymptotic spectrum. Those are substantive model-level constraints.

final_claim: For the Dong--Wang four-dimensional flow with \(b,c>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[xy]=b\) and \(b\mathbb E[z]=-c\mathbb E[y^2]<0\); no compact invariant set lies entirely in \(z\ge0\), and every compactly supported ergodic invariant measure satisfies the exact Lyapunov-sum law \(\sum_{j=1}^4\lambda_j=-a-c-(kc/b)\mathbb E[y^2]\).
limitations: The strict sign conclusions assume \(b>0\) and \(c>0\).
The Lyapunov-sum conclusion is for compactly supported ergodic invariant measures.
The theorem supplies necessary recurrent-statistics constraints, not existence, uniqueness or hyperchaos of a particular attractor.
